books.section: B. Politics, Big Business, and Corruption in the Gilded Age

stimulus.text:
Presidential elections, 1876–1896. Popular vote shares and electoral votes for the leading candidates.

| Year | Candidate | Party | Popular vote | Electoral votes |
|---|---|---|---|---:|
| 1876 | Rutherford B. Hayes | Republican | 48.0% | 185 |
| 1876 | Samuel J. Tilden | Democratic | 51.0% | 184 |
| 1880 | James A. Garfield | Republican | 48.3% | 214 |
| 1880 | Winfield S. Hancock | Democratic | 48.2% | 155 |
| 1884 | Grover Cleveland | Democratic | 48.9% | 219 |
| 1884 | James G. Blaine | Republican | 48.3% | 182 |
| 1888 | Benjamin Harrison | Republican | 47.8% | 233 |
| 1888 | Grover Cleveland | Democratic | 48.6% | 168 |
| 1892 | Grover Cleveland | Democratic | 46.0% | 277 |
| 1892 | Benjamin Harrison | Republican | 43.0% | 145 |
| 1892 | James B. Weaver | People’s Party | 8.5% | 22 |
| 1896 | William McKinley | Republican | 51.0% | 271 |
| 1896 | William Jennings Bryan | Democratic | 46.7% | 176 |

In 1896 the People’s Party also nominated Bryan.
stimulus.source_note: Presidential election returns, 1876–1896, American Presidency Project (via the Gilder Lehrman Institute). Popular vote shares rounded to one decimal place.

stem: What does James B. Weaver's result in 1892 best show about the People's Party?

options.text: It won the presidency by carrying the South and the West
options.misconception: Weaver finished third with 22 electoral votes, far from winning.

options.text: It drew its votes mainly from eastern industrial cities
options.misconception: The Populists drew strength from farmers in the South and West, not eastern cities.

options.text: It agreed with the major parties on the money question
options.misconception: The Populists demanded free silver, which the major parties resisted.

options.text: It broke the two-party hold enough to win electoral votes

rationales.A: Weaver took 8.5 percent and 22 votes, a strong third-place showing, not a win.
rationales.B: Populist strength lay with southern and western farmers, not city voters.
rationales.C: Free silver was the Populists' demand against the gold-standard parties.
rationales.D: A third party winning 22 electoral votes shows the two-party hold cracking.
rationales.general:
Put Weaver's row beside the other 1892 rows.
1. Weaver took 8.5 percent of the popular vote and 22 electoral votes.
2. No other third-party candidate in the table won any electoral votes.
3. Winning electoral votes means carrying whole states, not just scattering votes.
4. Background from the books: the Populists spoke for farmers the major parties had ignored.
Remember: electoral votes show where a movement carried states, not just votes.
